auditType: Quality hardening audit (test suite, repository layout, persistence behaviour)

findings.title: Audit log date-range query not translatable by SQLite provider
findings.description: AuditLogRepository.GetByDateRangeAsync filtered on DateTimeOffset with >= / <=. The EF Core SQLite provider stores DateTimeOffset as TEXT and cannot translate range comparisons, so the query threw InvalidOperationException at runtime (surfaced by the new storage test suite).
findings.impact: Audit trail filtering by date range would fail for any caller (reports, dashboards, compliance views).
findings.recommendation: Apply the window in memory (AsNoTracking -> Where -> OrderBy) with an explanatory comment; revisit with a DateTimeOffset value converter + migration if audit volume grows.
findings.evidence: SOCpit.Storage.Tests.AuditLogRepositoryTests.AddAndQuery_Work failed before the fix; passes after it.

findings.title: Read-only repository queries were inconsistently tracked
findings.description: Vulnerability, incident, evidence, host, network, user and audit repositories executed read-only queries on tracked DbSet instances, while other repositories used AsNoTracking. Mixed tracking invites stale-entity and change-tracker conflicts inside a shared UnitOfWork.
findings.impact: Potential 'entity already tracked' exceptions and unnecessary memory pressure in long-lived sessions.
findings.recommendation: Use AsNoTracking() for all read-only query paths.
findings.evidence: Repositories now consistently call AsNoTracking() for filter queries.

findings.title: Repository layout diverged from the documented architecture
findings.description: Six of eight repository implementations lived inside VulnerabilityRepository.cs and all nine repository interfaces were declared in IThreatRepository.cs, while ARCHITECTURE.md / DELIVERY_SUMMARY.md / NEO-ACTIONS.md documented one file per repository.
findings.impact: Documentation and code disagreed; navigation and review were harder than necessary.
findings.recommendation: One file per repository interface and implementation.
findings.evidence: src/SOCpit.Application/Repositories and src/SOCpit.Storage/Repositories each contain one file per repository.

findings.title: Test coverage claim was not substantiated by the repository
findings.description: Previous deliveries reported a comprehensive test suite, but the repository contained a single test file with 5 facts; the packaged ZIP even contained empty SOCpit.Application.Tests / SOCpit.Import.Tests folders. No coverage number was measurable.
findings.impact: Regression risk for every layer below the UI; acceptance evidence did not match the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Build real per-layer test projects, measure coverage in CI and publish the numbers.
findings.evidence: 261 tests across 4 projects; 3204/3419 lines = 93.71% line coverage reported by the CI coverage gate.

findings.title: README feature list overstated implemented functionality
findings.description: README claimed MITRE ATT&CK mapping, CVSS v3.1 vectors, CSV/XML import-export and RBAC roles (Operator, Auditor, ReadOnly) that do not exist in the domain model or the import layer.
findings.impact: Users could expect features that the application does not provide.
findings.recommendation: Document what the code actually implements.
findings.evidence: README.md feature list now matches SOCpit.Core enums and SOCpit.Import capabilities.

findings.title: No automated quality gate on coverage
findings.description: CI built, tested and packaged the application but did not measure or enforce code coverage, so coverage could regress silently.
findings.impact: Quality regressions would not be detected until manual review.
findings.recommendation: Collect XPlat Code Coverage, publish the summary and fail the build below a floor.
findings.evidence: Workflow step 'Coverage quality gate' with COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=85; current measured value 93.71%.
